rules.sentence: Renal cell neoplasia represents a heterogeneous group of tumors with distinct histopathologic, genetic, and clinical features ranging from benign to high-grade malignant (Table 114-3).
Papillary tumors tend to be bilateral and multifocal.
Chromophobe tumors have a more indolent clinical course, and oncocytomas are considered benign neoplasms.

Clear cell tumors, the predominant histology, are found in >80% of patients who develop metastases.
Clear cell tumors arise from the epithelial cells of the proximal tubules and usually show chromosome 3p deletions.
Deletions of 3p21–26 (where the VHL gene maps) are identified in patients with familial as well as sporadic tumors.
